about: A demo run, replayed from a live gpt-6-luna run (1015-142718-94ab) at about 25x speed. The planner's question and every agent's edits and reports are that run's; in the live run the owner tried all ten model families, and here you choose. The tests, checks and budget caps run for real on a fresh copy of repo/. Code identical to the live run's gets the score already measured for it, from scores.json (LUCIDITY_RESCORE=1 recomputes them all, about 10 minutes, mostly the SVM); any other code is scored for real. Agents were refused the held-out years; only Lucidity scored them. Returns, the Fama-French factors and momentum, and each industry's firm count, size and book-to-market are from Kenneth French's Data Library (49 industry portfolios, built from CRSP).
title: Stock returns

card.ask: Which industries beat the median next month? From past returns, factors, size and value.
card.why: Say 50% for every industry. Log loss charges 0.693 a row for that, so 0.693 means no skill. Plain regression on every column, factors included, does slightly worse.

blurb: A model predicts which of 49 industries will beat the median industry next month, from past returns, the Fama-French factors and momentum, and each industry's size, firm count and book-to-market. A coin flip scores 0.6931 log loss, so the goal is 0.6917. Ten kinds of model are tried at once, one agent each, tuning on 2010-2016. Lucidity scores every attempt on 2017-2026, years the agents never see, and recommends the best, or tells you none of them works.
split: Trained on 1971-2009, tuned on 2010-2016, tested on 2017-2026. Agents never see the test years; only Lucidity scores them.

about_repo: bundled industry-return model: 49 industries, monthly 1970-2026, Fama-French factors and industry size/value data, logistic regression, evals/score.py
commit_message: stockkit: last month + last year returns, logistic regression, 49 industries 1970-2026, Fama-French factors and industry size/value data, evals/score.py
goal: Get held-out log loss to 0.6917 or lower (a coin flip scores 0.6931) for predicting which industries beat the median next month, without accuracy dropping. Tune on the dev split. The repo has Fama-French factors, momentum, and each industry's firm count, size and book-to-market alongside the returns; each agent may use them as inputs. Ask the owner which model families to try (plain linear regression with predictions clipped to 1-99%, plain logistic regression, naive Bayes, lasso logistic regression, ridge logistic regression, kNN, SVM, a single decision tree, random forest, boosted trees), then build each one in parallel and keep the best. Give each agent up to 4 rounds.

plan.summary: Build and compare the owner-selected probability model families using the dev split, keeping the best model that meets held-out log-loss and accuracy requirements. The model-family choice is a judgment call, so the owner’s selections determine which parallel attempts run.

nodes.title: Compare selected model families and retain the winner
nodes.prompt: For each owner-selected model family, implement an independent candidate in stockkit/model.py (or a small appropriate helper), using only features available through the existing Tracker protocol. Tune hyperparameters and probability calibration using the dev split only. Compare candidates using dev log loss and accuracy; choose a model intended to achieve held-out log loss <= 0.6917 without accuracy below the repo baseline. Do not use heldout results for tuning; leave the selected implementation as the default model.
strategies: Plain linear regression (clipped 1–99%). Implement ordinary linear regression with outputs clipped to [0.01, 0.99] and a probability-compatible predict_proba interface.
Plain logistic regression. Implement plain logistic regression, tune sensible scaling and regularization on dev.
Naive Bayes. Implement a suitable naive Bayes classifier and tune its smoothing on dev.
Lasso logistic regression. Implement L1-regularized logistic regression; tune regularization and scaling on dev.
Ridge logistic regression. Implement L2-regularized logistic regression; tune regularization and scaling on dev.
kNN. Implement k-nearest neighbors with scaled inputs; tune neighbor count and probability smoothing on dev.
SVM. Implement SVM with probability outputs or calibration; tune kernel and regularization on dev.
Single decision tree. Implement a pruned decision tree classifier; tune depth and leaf size on dev.
Random forest. Implement random forest classification; tune depth, leaf size, and ensemble size on dev.
Boosted trees. Implement a gradient-boosted tree classifier available in the installed stack; tune depth, learning rate, and regularization on dev.

questions.question: Which model families should agents implement and compare? Select one or more; each selected family will be tried as a separate parallel approach.

options.label: Plain linear regression (clipped 1–99%)
options.note: Simple baseline; clipped predictions can be poorly calibrated.
options.approach: Implement ordinary linear regression with outputs clipped to [0.01, 0.99] and a probability-compatible predict_proba interface.

options.label: Plain logistic regression
options.note: A regularized logistic baseline is often robust for this small, correlated feature set.
options.approach: Implement plain logistic regression, tune sensible scaling and regularization on dev.

options.label: Naive Bayes
options.note: Fast and simple, but feature dependence may limit probability quality.
options.approach: Implement a suitable naive Bayes classifier and tune its smoothing on dev.

options.label: Lasso logistic regression
options.note: Can select among correlated inputs and reduce overfit.
options.approach: Implement L1-regularized logistic regression; tune regularization and scaling on dev.

options.label: Ridge logistic regression
options.note: Shrinkage can improve calibration with correlated signals.
options.approach: Implement L2-regularized logistic regression; tune regularization and scaling on dev.

options.label: kNN
options.note: Can capture local patterns, but requires careful scaling and calibration.
options.approach: Implement k-nearest neighbors with scaled inputs; tune neighbor count and probability smoothing on dev.

options.label: SVM
options.note: Margins or an RBF kernel may capture nonlinearities, with probability calibration needed.
options.approach: Implement SVM with probability outputs or calibration; tune kernel and regularization on dev.

options.label: Single decision tree
options.note: Readable nonlinear baseline, though likely to overfit without pruning.
options.approach: Implement a pruned decision tree classifier; tune depth and leaf size on dev.

options.label: Random forest
options.note: Averaged trees can model interactions, but probability calibration may need tuning.
options.approach: Implement random forest classification; tune depth, leaf size, and ensemble size on dev.

options.label: Boosted trees
options.note: Flexible interactions may help, but require conservative tuning to avoid overfit.
options.approach: Implement a gradient-boosted tree classifier available in the installed stack; tune depth, learning rate, and regularization on dev.

modelsa-r1.report: I replaced the default model with ordinary least-squares linear regression whose predictions are clipped to 1–99%, with a `predict_proba` interface. Tests pass, but the conditions do not: dev log loss is 0.6934 and accuracy is 0.5102, and the held-out score was refused by the eval script.

modelsa-r2.report: I expanded the causal return-history features and kept the model as clipped ordinary least-squares regression; the expanded features performed worse on dev, so I retained a narrower set of return-history features. Tests pass, but the done-when conditions do not: dev log loss is 0.6934, and the held-out score was withheld.
modelsa-r2.changed: Added prior-return inputs at 3, 6, and 36 months; standardized model inputs before linear regression, keeping probability clipping at 0.01–0.99.

modelsa-r3.report: I retained the clipped ordinary least-squares model and reverted the expanded features because they worsened dev results; the dev log loss is 0.6934 and accuracy is 0.5094. Tests pass, but the score conditions are not verified: the held-out eval was refused, and the available dev results do not demonstrate the required thresholds.
